characterList.description: A man with short dark hair wearing a dark suit and a light blue shirt, standing behind a wooden podium.
characterList.name: Speaker

content_metadata.description: A speaker delivers a passionate speech advocating for museums to adapt to the digital age, using engaging visuals and rhetorical questions to highlight the necessity of embracing new technologies and collaborative approaches.

qAndA.answer: The speaker says, 'World's on fire, and we fan it. It's in trouble.'
qAndA.question: What metaphor does the speaker use to describe the urgent state of the world?
What animal is shown on the book cover related to programming language C?

qAndA.answer: He encourages them to 'Jack the Museum.'
qAndA.question: What specific action does the speaker urge museums to take?

qAndA.answer: The Lego heads represent the collective power and potential of connected individuals to build something new and innovative, just as Lego bricks can be assembled in countless ways.
qAndA.question: What is the significance of the image of Lego heads in the context of the speaker's message?

qAndA.answer: He contrasts the slow and limited reach of sailboats in the past with the fast-paced and globalized nature of the internet age, suggesting that museums need to adopt new approaches that scale to meet the demands of the present.
qAndA.question: How does the speaker use the analogy of the "age of sail" to highlight the need for change in museums?

activities.description: Speaker delivers a speech about the age of sail.

narrativeProgression.description: The speaker introduces the concept of the 'age of sail' and its historical significance.
The speaker emphasizes the reliance on sailboats for various purposes in the past.
The speaker playfully suggests that only a fool would choose to row in the age of sail.

activities.description: Speaker transitions to a discussion of modern technology.

scenes.contextualRelevance: Nuanced perspective on tradition and progress.

narrativeProgression.description: The speaker acknowledges the appeal of slower ways of life, using the analogy of reading a book over digital content.
He parallels 'slow, dirty travel' of a rowboat with intellectual exploration of less-traveled paths.
He asserts that grand tasks require a faster, more forceful approach, symbolized by the propeller.

props.name: Images of a rowboat, a couple in a rowboat, and a large ship propeller on the projector screen

scenes.thematicElements: Contrast between traditional and modern approaches.
scenes.title: Modern Technology vs. Slow Travel

videoEditingDetails.description: Images change less frequently for a more focused viewing experience.

activities.description: Speaker highlights the need for action and change on a global scale.

scenes.contextualRelevance: Critique of museums and call for accessibility.

narrativeProgression.description: The speaker calls for action and progress, using metaphors like 'jamming' and 'manning and womaning'.
He uses the image of a 'hot-packed planet' on fire to symbolize the critical state of the world.
He criticizes outdated tools and methods, calling them a waste of time.
He challenges traditional institutions like museums, suggesting they can become stagnant.

props.name: Images of a planet earth, a museum interior, and stacks of books on the projector screen

scenes.thematicElements: Need for impactful action and innovation.
scenes.title: A Call for Global Action and Change

He highlights the power of new technologies to bring change.
He encourages embracing 'network action'.

youtube_description:
Michael Edson of the Smithsonian Institution in Washington DC at Wikimedia UK's GLAM-Wiki 2013 at the British Library, London. In this video he performs an incredible poem inspired by openness.

His main presentation can be seen here: http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wp_BdHDZW68
